last_transition_reason: The proof correctly uses the hypothesis floor(k t) = k - 1 for all 1 <= k <= n, rewrites the sum as n - H_n, and concludes E_n(t) = H_n - 1. This matches the lemma statement exactly and introduces no dependency issues.
latest_nl_proof:
Let H_n := \sum_{k=1}^n \frac{1}{k}, the usual harmonic number. Assume that for every integer k with 1 \le k \le n we have \lfloor kt\rfloor = k-1. In particular, taking k=n gives \lfloor nt\rfloor = n-1. Therefore
\[
E_n(t)=\lfloor nt\rfloor-\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{\lfloor kt\rfloor}{k}
=(n-1)-\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{k-1}{k}.
\]
Now \(\frac{k-1}{k}=1-\frac1k\), so
\[
\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{k-1}{k}=\sum_{k=1}^n \left(1-\frac1k\right)=n-\sum_{k=1}^n \frac1k=n-H_n.
\]
Substituting this into the expression for \(E_n(t)\) yields
\[
E_n(t)=(n-1)-(n-H_n)=H_n-1.
\]
Thus the conclusion holds.
